meta.location: The hill Onidah, in the land of Antionum
principles: An atonement that must be infinite
Prayer that has to reach the poor

world_behind.title: Amulek picks up mid-sermon
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has Alma sit down on the ground and Amulek stand. The two chapters are one discourse handed from one preacher to the other in the middle.

world_behind.title: He knows these people were taught
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says these things were taught bountifully before their dissension. Amulek is arguing with people who once held what he holds.

world_behind.title: He names the question exactly
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says the great question in their minds is whether the word is in the Son of God or whether there shall be no Christ. Alma 31 had them denying it from the stand.

world_behind.title: Amulek's own credential is personal
world_behind.text: Verse 8 has him testify of himself that he knows Christ shall come. Alma 10 gave his account of the angel; here he offers the knowledge without retelling the story.

world_behind.title: The law of Moses is treated as pointing
world_behind.text: Verses 13 and 14 say the whole meaning of the law points to the great and last sacrifice. Alma 25 had already explained why the converts still kept it.

world_behind.title: The prayer list is a working life
world_behind.text: Fields, flocks, houses, household, crops, closets, secret places, wilderness, morning, midday, evening. Every item belongs to people who work outdoors and own little.

world_behind.title: Charity is made the test of the prayer
world_behind.text: Verse 28 says a prayer is vain if the needy are turned away. Amulek is speaking to poor people and still tells them to impart of their substance if they have it.

words.text: Without limit or end. The phrase "infinite and eternal" (v. 10) occurs twice in this record, both in this chapter. Amulek uses it to rule out every finite substitute he has just listed: no man, no beast, no fowl, and no human sacrifice.

The smallest stroke of a letter. The pairing with jot occurs once in this record and comes from the Sermon on the Mount, where nothing passes from the law until all is fulfilled. Amulek uses it to say the law is completed, not thrown away.

Surrounds, closes around. The word occurs once in scripture, in the phrase about mercy encircling the repentant in the arms of safety. Amulek reaches for an image of enclosure to describe what mercy does once justice is satisfied.

Those who purify metal. The word occurs once in scripture. Amulek says the uncharitable are as dross that refiners cast out, which picks up the word Mormon used in Alma 32 of these same people and turns it around on anyone who will not give.

Treated at Alma 13:27, where Alma begs the people of Ammonihah not to put off repentance. Amulek is speaking to a different audience with the same word, and the two chapters are the record's only uses of it.
Alert, keeping guard. The record uses it twice, here and in Moroni 6, where the church watches over its members. Amulek attaches it to continual prayer as protection against being overpowered.

phrases.term: He sat down upon the ground, and Amulek arose
phrases.text: Mormon records the handoff physically. Alma takes the ground and Amulek takes the standing. Alma 31 had described worship that required one man alone on a platform, and this pair trades places on a hill.

phrases.term: These things were taught unto you bountifully before your dissension from among us
phrases.text: Amulek reminds them what they used to know. The Zoramites are dissenters, so the argument is a recovery, and he says so before saying anything else.

phrases.term: It must be an infinite and eternal sacrifice
phrases.text: The center of the chapter. Amulek rules out man, beast, and fowl, and says nothing finite will answer. Verse 12 gives his reason: the law requires the life of the one who owes it.

phrases.term: This is the whole meaning of the law, every whit pointing to that great and last sacrifice
phrases.text: Amulek gives an interpretation of the entire Mosaic system in one sentence. Every part of it points at one event. When the event arrives the law is fulfilled by it.

phrases.term: Mercy can satisfy the demands of justice, and encircles them in the arms of safety
phrases.text: The relation between the two is stated as a transaction with a condition attached. Mercy satisfies justice for the person who exercises faith unto repentance, and verse 16 says the one who does not stands exposed to the whole law.

phrases.term: Cry unto him when ye are in your fields, yea, over all your flocks
phrases.text: The first of eight places. Amulek is answering the same question Alma answered with Zenos, and his list is longer and more agricultural. He is telling landless people to pray over work.

phrases.term: Ye must pour out your souls in your closets, and your secret places, and in your wilderness
phrases.text: After the public and practical list, the private one. The wilderness here is a person's own, which puts solitary prayer alongside prayer over crops as equally required.

phrases.term: When you do not cry unto the Lord, let your hearts be full, drawn out in prayer unto him continually
phrases.text: The instruction covers the time between prayers. Amulek is describing a disposition, and he extends it to the welfare of those around them.

phrases.term: If ye do not any of these things, behold, your prayer is vain
phrases.text: The chapter's hardest turn. After nine verses on how to pray, Amulek says the whole of it counts for nothing if the needy are turned away. He names the naked, the sick, and the afflicted.

phrases.term: This life is the time for men to prepare to meet God
phrases.text: The sentence most often quoted from this chapter. Verse 32 pairs it with labor: the day of this life is the day to perform them, and verse 33 says the night follows when no labor can be done.

phrases.term: That ye do not revile against those who do cast you out because of your exceeding poverty
phrases.text: The last instruction, and it is about the people who excluded them. Amulek's reason is practical: reviling would make them sinners like the ones who threw them out.

verses.label: v. 1–7
verses.title: Amulek stands
verses.text: Alma sits down and Amulek begins. He says they cannot be ignorant of what they were taught before they dissented, names the great question as whether there shall be a Christ, and summarizes Alma's witnesses: Zenos, Zenock, and Moses.

verses.label: v. 8–14
verses.title: The infinite sacrifice
verses.text: He testifies of himself that Christ will come and atone. An atonement is required or all mankind perishes. It cannot be man or beast or fowl, and no man's blood atones for another's, so it must be infinite and eternal. Then the law is fulfilled, every jot and tittle, every whit of it pointing here.

verses.label: v. 15–18
verses.title: Mercy and justice
verses.text: The intent of the last sacrifice is to bring about the bowels of mercy, which overpower justice and give men means to have faith unto repentance. Mercy satisfies justice and encircles the repentant; the unrepentant face the whole law. Cry for mercy, for he is mighty to save.

verses.label: v. 19–27
verses.title: Where to cry
verses.text: Humble yourselves and continue in prayer. Fields, flocks, houses, household, morning and midday and evening, against enemies, against the devil, over crops, over increase. Then closets, secret places, wilderness, and hearts drawn out continually for your own welfare and everyone else's.

verses.label: v. 28–29
verses.title: The condition
verses.text: All of that is vain if the needy and naked are turned away and the sick are unvisited. Those who do not remember to be charitable are as dross the refiners cast out and men tread underfoot.

verses.label: v. 30–36
verses.title: Now is the time
verses.text: Bring fruit unto repentance and harden not your hearts, for now is the day of salvation. This life is the time to prepare and to labor, and the night comes when no labor is possible. The spirit that possesses you at death possesses you after, and the Lord dwells in the hearts of the righteous.

verses.label: v. 37–41
verses.title: The closing charge
verses.text: Work out your salvation, deny the coming of Christ no more, contend not against the Holy Ghost, take his name, worship in whatever place you are, live in daily thanksgiving, be watchful unto prayer, and bear afflictions without reviling those who cast you out.

chapter.title: Two preachers, one sermon
chapter.text: Alma sits and Amulek stands without a break in the argument. Alma 32 and 33 prepared the ground and Alma 34 supplies the doctrine that the seed was carrying.

chapter.title: The atonement is argued from law
chapter.text: Amulek's case is that a just law requires the life of the one who owes it, so no finite substitute answers. He builds a doctrinal necessity out of a legal principle his hearers already accept.

chapter.title: The law of Moses is closed, not cancelled
chapter.text: Every jot and tittle fulfilled, every whit pointing to one sacrifice. The system ends by arriving rather than by failing.

chapter.title: The prayer list is built for their lives
chapter.text: Fields, flocks, crops, increase, household, three times a day. Amulek gives poor agricultural workers a practice that fits the day they actually have.

chapter.title: He then says prayer alone is worthless
chapter.text: Verse 28 undoes the preceding nine verses for anyone who will not give. The structure is deliberate, and the reversal is the point.

chapter.title: He asks the poor to give
chapter.text: Impart of your substance, if ye have, to those who stand in need. The qualification is honest and the instruction is not withdrawn.

chapter.title: Time is the chapter's other subject
chapter.text: Now is the day, this life is the time, the night comes, do not put it off. Amulek treats mortality as a working day with an end.

chapter.title: The last word is about their enemies
chapter.text: Do not revile the people who cast you out. Amulek closes a sermon about infinite sacrifice by telling the excluded not to become like those who excluded them.

applications.title: Pray over the work in front of you
applications.text: Amulek names crops, flocks, and household by name. Take the specific thing you are responsible for this week and pray about it by name rather than in general.

applications.title: Check your prayer against your giving
applications.text: Amulek says the practice is vain if the needy are turned away. Look at the last month of what you actually gave and visited, and put it beside what you have been praying about.

applications.title: Give from what you have, not what you wish you had
applications.text: He told poor people to impart of their substance if they have it. Rather than waiting until you can give properly, give the amount that is actually available.

applications.title: Do not become like the people who shut you out
applications.text: Amulek tells them reviling would make them sinners like their excluders. When you have been treated badly, decide in advance what you will not do in return.

questions.text: What did I once know clearly that I have quietly stopped holding?
What is the great question actually in my mind right now?
Have I understood mercy as something that satisfies justice or as something that ignores it?
Where is my secret place, and when was I last in it?
Whose need have I stepped over on my way to pray?
If this life is the time to prepare, what am I preparing?
Who has cast me out, and what have I been saying about them?
